resources.string: No plants yet. Tap + to add a plant, then add its inverters, batteries and meters.

This removes the plant, its devices and its plant history (solar, home, battery, grid) from the app. Nothing on the devices changes. Each device\'s own recorded data is kept: add the same device again, to any plant, and it comes back.
Also delete the devices\' recorded data
Blank: this tablet’s own network. E.g. 192.168.1 (all its addresses), 192.168.1.0/24, or one address such as 192.168.1.200.
Not a network: e.g. 192.168.1, 192.168.1.0/24 or 192.168.1.200 (at most 254 addresses)

Search network tries Modbus TCP port 502 on every address of this Wi-Fi network, then identifies what answered (the named inverters and the ModbusSpec devices that can tell what they are). Every open port is listed, also unrecognised ones. Extended search also tries the other ports devices use (503, 1502, 6502, 8899, 4196 …) and takes longer. Devices that can’t be recognised are added by hand.
Only add standalone batteries here. A battery on a hybrid inverter is already read through the inverter, and adding it again would count it twice.
A meter at the grid connection replaces the inverters\' grid values. A PV meter adds production (e.g. an inverter without communication); a consumer sub-meter shows a single load.
Consumers are shown as parts of the home load. They don\'t change the plant totals: the grid meter or the balance already includes them.
RS485 gateway in transparent mode (Modbus RTU over TCP)
For gateways that pass the RS485 bytes on as they are (Waveshare, USR and Elfin often ship like this, e.g. on port 4196 or 8899). Leave it off when the gateway converts to Modbus TCP.
Several devices behind the same gateway share its IP address and port, and differ by unit id.

Gateway software 7 and later needs a token: create an owner token (valid one year) at entrez.enphaseenergy.com for this gateway\'s serial number and paste it here. When it expires the device shows \"token expired or missing\".

The user password is the unit\'s MAC address, lowercase without colons (e.g. 001122aabbcc). Find it in your router\'s list of connected devices, or on a computer with `ip neigh` after pinging the unit. Android doesn\'t let apps look it up.
If the meter is wired the other way round (export shown as import, or a PV meter showing 0 while producing), tick this.
SunSpec doesn\'t define which way the meter counts. If the dashboard shows export while you\'re drawing from the grid (or the other way round), tick this.

Unit id 1 for an inverter behind an SDongle or SmartLogger (its address there); 0 when connecting to the inverter\'s own WLAN or FE port. Modbus TCP must be enabled on the SDongle (FusionSolar app: Communication Configuration).

TRIO inverters only have RS485. Connect them through an RS485 to Ethernet gateway set to \"Modbus TCP to RTU\" (19200 baud, 8N1 by default); enter the gateway\'s IP and port, and the inverter\'s RS485 address as unit id. Several TRIOs on one bus share the gateway. At night the inverter switches off and shows as sleeping.

Use the inverter\'s own LAN port or a WiNet-S / WiNet-S2 / Logger1000 on Ethernet (not iHomeManager). Port 502, unit id = the inverter\'s Modbus address (default 1; behind a WiNet use the address its web page lists). Hybrid or string model is detected. Grid and home values need a Sungrow smart meter.

Modbus is off by default: in the inverter\'s web interface (as Installer) set Device Parameters → External Communication → Modbus → TCP Server to Yes, port 502. Unit id 3. Add every inverter by its own IP. Grid power needs an SMA energy meter on the device; a Sunny Island reports house load but not solar, so add the PV inverters as well.

These inverter-chargers have an RS232 port (RJ45 or DB9), not Modbus. Connect it to an RS232 to TCP gateway (e.g. Elfin EW11) using the cable that came with the inverter: serial 2400 baud, 8N1, no flow control; network side TCP server, port 8899, transparent mode (not Modbus). The app only sends read commands. These units don\'t measure grid power.
SunSpec Modbus TCP, port 502, unit id 1 (enable Modbus/SunSpec in the inverter).
Through a VSN300 / VSN700 logger or a native SunSpec inverter: port 502; unit id 247 for the logger, else the inverter\'s Aurora address (often 2).
Enable Modbus in EMA Manager (ECU-R firmware 1.3.7 / 2.0.2, ECU-C C1.1.3 or later). Add one device per microinverter: unit id = its Modbus address from EMA Manager. Port 502.

The CDD collects the data of the ABB MICRO-0.3 microinverters by radio and shows it on its own web page. Enter the CDD\'s IP address, port 80; no password is needed. The app shows the plant total and each microinverter, and the CDD\'s alarm log.
SunSpec Modbus TCP, port 502, unit id 10 (factory default). Power has 100 W steps over SunSpec.
Reads the whole XW system from the Conext Gateway / Insight Home: port 503, unit id 1.
Modbus TCP port 1502, unit id 71 (enable Modbus in the inverter\'s web interface).
Modbus TCP through the inverter\'s dongle: port 502, unit id 1. Ingeteam allows one client and asks for at least 1 s between requests.
CPS inverters speak Modbus RTU (9600 8N1): use an RS485 to Ethernet gateway in \"Modbus TCP to RTU\" mode. 275 / 350 kW units also have Modbus TCP on port 502. Unit id = RS485 address (default 1).
Modbus TCP, or RTU (9600 baud) through a gateway. Port 502, unit id 1.
EM24 Ethernet: the meter\'s IP, port 502. EM300 / EM210 / EM24-DIN: an RS485 gateway (9600 8N1; old EM24-DIN 4800 or 9600), unit id = meter address (default 1). The model is detected.
RS485 gateway in Modbus TCP to RTU mode: SDM630 9600 8N1, SDM120 2400 8N1 (factory defaults); unit id = meter address (default 1).
RS485 gateway in Modbus TCP to RTU mode, 9600 8E1; unit id = meter address (default 1).
Set the meter\'s RS485 protocol to Modbus first; then an RS485 gateway at the meter\'s baud rate and parity, unit id = its Modbus address.
Modbus TCP port 502, unit id = the device\'s Modbus address (default 1). A 96RM without Ethernet needs an RS485 gateway.
RS485 Modbus RTU through a Modbus TCP gateway; unit id = the meter\'s address set on its display.
Modbus TCP port 502 (or the port set on the device), unit id 1.
In the KSEM web interface enable the Modbus TCP slave without TLS. Port 502, unit id 1.
Enable Modbus in the Shelly web interface. Port 502, unit id 1.
Set DIP switch DSW1.3 to ON (firmware c-series 3.10.16 / x-series 1.11 or later); don\'t use the UDP interface at the same time. Port 502, unit id 255. Read only.
Needs the Active Load Balancing licence; in ACE Service Installer set the data source to Energy Management System, Modbus TCP/IP, and switch on \"Allow reading\". Port 502; unit id 1 or 2 = socket.
In the wallbox\'s web interface switch on \"Modbus TCP Server\" (ECU software 5.12 or later). Port 502; a second connector answers on port 503, add it as its own device.
Enable Modbus in the go-e app: Internet → Advanced settings → Modbus. Port 502, unit id 1.
In the heater\'s web interface set the control type to Modbus TCP. Port 502, unit id 1. Read only.

Needs an ISG web / plus / Connect with the Modbus TCP/IP software extension. Port 502, unit id 1. Read only: temperatures, state and the daily and total electrical energy (the ISG reports no live power).
Enable menu 7.5.9 \"Modbus TCP/IP\" on the heat pump (software 2.2.1 or later); \"Reading Modbus only\" is recommended. Port 502. The heat pump only accepts clients on private networks.
Needs the TopTronic E Modbus gateway (software V2.38 or later), for heat pumps with WFA (UltraSource, Belaria pro). Read slowly, every 30 s. Port 502, unit id 1.
Reads the whole system (PV, battery, grid, consumption) through the pre-installed FEMS App \"Modbus/TCP Read Access\": port 502, unit id 1.
On the GX enable Settings → Integrations → Modbus TCP server (older Venus OS: Settings → Services → Modbus TCP). Port 502, unit id 100 = the whole installation (PV, consumption, grid, battery).

Growatt hybrids speak Modbus RTU on RS485: use an RS485 to Ethernet gateway in \"Modbus TCP to RTU\" mode (9600 baud, 8N1). Unit id = the inverter\'s communication address (default 1). Grid and home values need the Growatt smart meter; Growatt doesn\'t report today\'s solar yield over this protocol.
Enable Modbus TCP in SetApp (or the LCD menu): wired LAN only, port 1502, device id 1. SolarEdge allows a single Modbus client. Meters connected to the inverter are read too.
For any inverter speaking SunSpec over Modbus TCP (e.g. SMA with SunSpec enabled: unit id 126). Reads the inverter, MPPT, battery and meter models the device offers.

Enable Modbus TCP in the inverter\'s web interface (Communication → Modbus: \"SunSpec Model Type\" float or int + SF both work); port 502, unit id 1. A Fronius Smart Meter at the grid connection is read through the inverter (unit id 200).

Enable Modbus TCP in the inverter\'s web interface (Settings → Modbus / SunSpec (TCP)); port 1502, unit id 71. With a master and slave (host and client) add each inverter as its own device of this plant: the app finds out which one has the battery and the energy meter.

This device can\'t report its model over Modbus: choose it here, so the right values are read.
Reads every register with function 03, then 04, without writing anything, and saves the traffic to a file in the app\'s folder.
Pass %1$d of %2$d · function %3$s · %4$d of %5$d requests · %6$d registers answered
Function %1$s stopped, no answer any more: %2$s
Answered: %1$d holding (03), %2$d input (04) registers, saved to %3$s

This sends the file %1$s (%2$s) to %3$s.\n\nIt contains the device’s name, IP address, port and unit id, and every request and answer of the sweep: all register values the device returned, which can include its serial number. Nothing else from the app is sent.
Not shown on the dashboard or the kiosk; still recorded in the fault log.
